sets.label: State of the Golden Gate Bridge (General adult, introductory)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Oregon is the state just north of California. The bridge is in San Francisco, California.
Correct. The Golden Gate Bridge crosses the entrance to San Francisco Bay in California.
Nevada is east of California and has no coast. The Golden Gate Bridge is on the California coast.
Washington State is in the Pacific Northwest, far north of the bridge, which is in California.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: No. The Indian Ocean is on the far side of the world and does not touch any U.S. state.
Yes. The Pacific Ocean lies along the western coast of the connected states.
No. The Arctic Ocean touches Alaska's north coast, not the connected states.
Yes. The Atlantic Ocean lies along the eastern coast of the connected states.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Jacksonville is a large city in northeastern Florida, but it is not the capital.
Fort Lauderdale is a coastal city in southeastern Florida, but it is not the capital.
Miami is a major city on the southeastern coast, but it is not the capital.
Correct. Tallahassee, in the Panhandle region, is the capital of Florida.

origin.author: READY builder

Bloomington is a city in central Illinois, but it is not the capital.
Chicago is the state's best-known city, but not the capital. The capital is in central Illinois.
Correct. Springfield is the capital of Illinois. Several other states have a Springfield too.

Yes. Iowa is in the Census Bureau's Midwest region.
No. The Census Bureau puts Montana in the West region.
No. The Census Bureau puts Arkansas in the South region.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Idaho is in the Census West region, in the Rocky Mountain area, not the South.
Vermont is in the Census Northeast region.
Correct. Georgia is in the Census Bureau's South region.
Iowa is in the Census Midwest region, in the north-central part of the country, not the South.

sets.label: Pick the Western state (General adult, basic)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. Montana is in the Census Bureau's West region, which includes the Mountain states.
Iowa is in the Census Midwest region, in the north-central part of the country, not the West.
Arkansas is in the Census South region, west of the Mississippi River but not in the West.
Georgia is in the Census South region, on the Atlantic side of the country, not the West.

sets.label: Interstate numbering (General adult, basic)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Loops around cities have three-digit numbers. A main two-digit odd route runs north-south.
Interstate numbers do not show whether a route stays in one state.
East-west routes use even numbers, such as 80 or 90.
Correct. Main Interstates with odd numbers run north-south, and those with even numbers run east-west.

sets.label: Biome of the Great Plains (General adult, basic)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. The Great Plains are mostly grassland, or prairie, with grasses suited to dry summers and wind.
Tropical rain forests need warm, wet weather all year, which does not fit the Great Plains.
Tundra is a cold treeless biome found in far northern places such as northern Alaska.
Deserts are much drier than the Plains. Parts of the Southwest are deserts.

sets.label: State split by a time-zone line (General adult, intermediate)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Iowa is entirely in the Central time zone.
Correct. Most of Texas is on Central time, but the El Paso area in the far west uses Mountain time.
Georgia is entirely in the Eastern time zone.
Colorado is entirely in the Mountain time zone.

sets.label: Census region of Delaware (General adult, intermediate)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Delaware is on the Atlantic coast, far east of the West region.
Correct. The Census Bureau groups Delaware, Maryland and Washington, D.C. with the South Atlantic states, in its South region.
Many people think of Delaware as Northeastern or Mid-Atlantic, and its location on the Atlantic seaboard supports that. It is not the Census assignment, though.
connections.notes: Cultural and geographic usage often places Delaware in the Northeast or Mid-Atlantic. The Census South assignment surprises many people. Marked ambiguous.

connections.feedback: Delaware is on the Atlantic coast, far east of the Midwest.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: No. Ohio comes from an Iroquoian word, often explained as meaning good river or great river.
Yes. Montana comes from a Spanish word for mountainous.
Yes. Nevada is Spanish for snow-covered, a name given to the Sierra Nevada.
Yes. Colorado is a Spanish word meaning colored red, probably for the red rock and river.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. A federal district means the national capital does not depend on a single state.
The land was once part of Maryland, but Maryland does not govern the city today. It is its own district.
No. Washington, D.C. was created as a federal district. It was never a state.
No. Washington, D.C. is a federal district, a separate category from territories such as Guam.

origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Yes. Congress and the federal government have their home in Washington, D.C.
No. D.C. sits on the Potomac River on the East Coast. Territories in the Pacific include Guam and American Samoa.
No. The district is separate from Maryland and is not governed by it.
Yes. Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state.

sets.label: Economy of the Central Valley (General adult, intermediate)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Deep-sea fishing is done on the coast and the ocean, not in an inland valley.
Correct. The Central Valley's flat land, long growing season and irrigation make it one of the country's major farming regions.
The valley is dry in summer. Rain forests are in other parts of the Pacific Northwest.
Ski resorts are in the nearby mountains, not on the valley floor.

sets.label: Independent country, not a territory (General adult, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: American Samoa is a U.S. territory. Its name is easy to confuse with the independent country of Samoa.
The Northern Mariana Islands are a U.S. commonwealth, a kind of territory, in the western Pacific.
Guam is a U.S. territory in the western Pacific.
Correct. Samoa is an independent country. American Samoa, a separate place, is a U.S. territory.

sets.label: Independent country, not a territory (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: American Samoa is a U.S. territory, and the name invites a mix-up with the neighboring country.
The Northern Mariana Islands are a U.S. commonwealth, a kind of territory, in the western Pacific.
Correct. Samoa is a sovereign country. American Samoa, to its east, is an unincorporated U.S. territory.
Guam is an unincorporated U.S. territory in the western Pacific.

sets.label: Meaning of the name Mississippi (General adult, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. The name comes from Ojibwe words that mean great river.
Many lakes are linked to Minnesota, near the river's source, but that is not the meaning of the name.
Muddy is a trait people link to the Missouri River, not the meaning of the Mississippi's name.
This is a popular translation and widely quoted, so it is not a careless answer. Many language experts prefer great river as the more direct meaning.
connections.notes: A very common translation in popular sources, but scholarly sources favor great river. Marked ambiguous so the feedback can explain, not mark it flatly wrong.

sets.label: Meaning of the name Mississippi (Adult enthusiast, expert)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: This is not the meaning. The name refers to the river itself, not to lakes.
Popular sources often give this, and it is a famous phrase, so it is a defensible answer. Language scholars generally prefer great river for the literal meaning.
connections.notes: Popular translation versus scholarly meaning. Marked ambiguous for expert level.

connections.feedback: This is not the meaning. The word for muddy is not part of the name.
Correct. The name is an English and French rendering of Ojibwe words for great river.
